title: Set Data Type
answer:
Sure, I'd be happy to help you with that! Here's a Python program that declares and uses a set to store a collection of unique values:

```python
# Declare a set to store unique values
unique_values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}

# Print the set to verify it contains unique values
print("The set is:", unique_values)

# Add more values to the set and print it again
unique_values.add(6)
print("The set now contains:", unique_values)

# Remove a value from the set and print it again
unique_values.remove(3)
print("The set after removing 3 is:", unique_values)
```

When you run this program, it will output:

```
The set is: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
The set now contains: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}
The set after removing 3 is: {1, 2, 4, 5, 6}
```

Sets in Python are unordered collections of unique elements. They automatically remove any duplicate values, making them an efficient choice for storing collections of unique items.
